title: Reporting inbound qualification and escalation synthesis
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: We receive a high volume of inbound console/reporting requests (usage exports, cost breakdowns, custom dashboards) from enterprise customers and CSMs. Currently requests are handled ad hoc by PMs and Solutions Engineers which leads to inconsistent SLAs, duplicate work, unclear data contracts, and under/over-scoped deliveries. Goal: define a lightweight qualification rubric + escalation flow that can be automated or semi-automated in the Console intake so requests are routed to the correct lane (self-serve template, engineering deliverable, analytics concierge, or professional services) with clear acceptance criteria, estimated cost/time, and tenant-aware consent checks.
acceptance_criteria: A1: A 6-question qualification form is defined that scores requests on scope, data sensitivity, frequency, and business impact
A2: Routing matrix maps score bands to lanes: Self-serve template, Low-effort PM work, Eng backlog (small), Dedicated Analytics Engagement (medium), PS/Custom integration (high)
A3: For Eng backlog lane, the intake creates a pre-filled Linear ticket with: sample dataset description, required fields, data contract checklist, desired SLA lane, and estimated engineering points
A4: Cost-estimation helper returns a ballpark monthly cost bucket (low/med/high) based on token/row volume and export frequency and surfaces to requestor and reviewer
A5: Tenant-aware consent and export gating checklist is included for any requests that include PII or cross-tenant joins
A6: Dashboard — mini view in Console for PM/SEs showing all pending reporting requests, their score, assigned lane, and time-since-submission
success_metrics: Reduce manual triage time per request from median 4 hours to <= 45 minutes
>40% of incoming requests auto-classified into self-serve or low-effort lanes within 14 days of rollout
Mean time to decision for enterprise reporting requests reduced to <= 3 business days
Fewer than 10% of routed requests are re-routed between lanes after initial assignment
Measure: Percentage of requests with complete data contract at initial intake increases to 80%
